inputs.source: Published HR policy documents (HR content team, two-person review before publish)

instructions.note: The boundary against giving legal advice is enforced only by a prompt instruction, not by any structural check on cap.chat_reply output. Low severity because the agent's only data source is published internal HR policy text, not legal content, which limits how far this can be pushed.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by IAM-level credential scoping outside the model. A more capable model cannot use access it was never granted. Only widening the grant defeats it.

controls.name: Reply bound to the authenticated requester's own session
controls.decay_rationale: The reply destination is taken from the authenticated session record, not chosen by the model, so it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial, pen-test verified
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer, independent of model behavior, and verified by penetration testing. Only removing or misconfiguring the network policy defeats it.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the chat client implementation, not the model. Closes a common covert-exfiltration channel regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Two-person review required to publish policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the HR publishing workflow outside the agent and outside the model. Defeated only if the review step itself is bypassed or removed.

controls.name: Model version pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: The model cannot silently become more capable. A change ticket gives a checkpoint to re-run this assessment before model_upgrade could defeat any dependent control.

controls.name: Prompt instruction against giving legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply. A more capable or adversarially prompted model could rationalize exceptions. Fails under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon.

controls.name: Audit logging of searches and replies
controls.decay_rationale: Detective control; would provide attribution and after-the-fact review regardless of model behavior. Not described in the provided artifacts.

findings.title: Internal policy content flows from the read-only index to the chat reply (I source to S2 sink)

attack_path.note: Agent reads the matched policy text
Matched policy text is quoted back to the authenticated requester's chat session

forecast.watch_signal: The policy index begins including confidential or case-specific HR content, or the agent's read credential is widened beyond the published-policy index, which would raise the sink's data sensitivity and defeat the least-privilege credential scoping.

evidence.observation: Policy index holds only published policies, classified internal; HR content team writes to it under two-person review before publish.
Only tool exposed is a read-only search over the policy index; no other egress-capable tool exists.
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session; the chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links, closing common covert exfiltration channels.
Agent credential is read only and scoped to the policy index, narrowing but not eliminating the disclosure of internal data through the chat reply sink.

recommendations.action: Add audit logging of search queries and the policy documents cited in replies so disclosures are attributable and reviewable.

If the policy index is ever expanded to include case-specific or confidential content, scope the agent's credential to a dedicated published-only subset and re-run this assessment before the expansion ships.

rating.rationale: The design exposes exactly one read-only tool over an internal, two-person-reviewed policy index, and a reply channel bound to the authenticated requester's own session, with no image rendering or auto link-fetch in the chat client. No untrusted input source exists anywhere in this design (the employee question is an authenticated direct instruction, and the policy content is internally authored under dual review), so none of the TC1-TC9 lethal-trifecta style combinations match. The one reportable path is the agent's intended function: internal policy text flows from the read-only index into the chat reply to the asking employee (I source, S2 sink), giving moderate inherent risk. This is reduced to low residual by two independent, structural controls that do not depend on model behavior: least-privilege credential scoping on the search tool and session-bound destination control on the reply. Neither control severs the path outright, because disclosure to the asker is the point of the tool, not a bypass; the residual sits at the rubric's floor. The forecast rises to moderate only under data_scope_expansion: if the policy index and the agent's credential both widen to more sensitive content, the sink reclassifies upward and the credential-scoping control is defeated, while the session-bound destination control still holds. Model_upgrade is not a material trigger today because the model is pinned behind a change ticket and the surviving controls are structural and independent rather than behavioral; the one dependent control (the prompt's legal-advice instruction) is unrelated to the disclosure path that drives this rating.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration (prompt.md, tools.json, and runtime notes) as described by the team, not observed runtime behavior or production logs.

No MCP/A2A protocol configuration, IaC, or source code was provided. Credential scoping, destination binding, and the no-render/no-autofetch property of the chat client are taken as declared in runtime notes except where explicitly stated as pen-test verified (network egress denial), so confidence on the unverified controls is medium.

No logging or audit configuration was described in the artifacts. Attributability of individual replies could not be assessed; this is recorded as a missing recommended control (ctrl.audit_logging_missing) rather than a confirmed gap.
